Definition: Integration of voter registration data for identity verification, demographic analysis, and service delivery targeting
Comments: ELECAM has operated a biometric voter card system since 2012 (Law No. 2012/001). Biometric voter kits procured for election administration per 2025 ID tech report. The system is electronic but integration with a unified data exchange layer not confirmed.
revision_notes: Original sources were weak: the datalaw.africa PDF concerns health-data informed consent and is entirely unrelated to electoral data; the idtechwire article is primarily about BUNEC/CRVS digitisation, not ELECAM's electoral register. Fresh searches confirm ELECAM runs its own computerised biometric register (SIGCE and Diaspora software, online verification portal) since 2012, and is currently deduplicating an ~8.2 million-voter biometric registry and procuring new biometric kits (2025). However, no authoritative source confirms this register is integrated into a cross-government data exchange/interoperability platform; the only integration signal is BUNEC's October 2025 statement that its new CRVS/UPIN system is 'expected to integrate' with existing ID and voter platforms, which is prospective rather than confirmed under-development integration. Evidence is too thin and contradictory to confidently choose between 'Not integrated' (1) and 'Planned' (2), so this is flagged for human review rather than asserting a value; the current Value Code of 3 (Under development) appears too high given available evidence.
revised_comments: ELECAM (Elections Cameroon) maintains a computerised, biometric electoral register through its SIGCE and Diaspora software systems, first introduced in 2012, with an online portal that allows voters to verify their registration details. ELECAM continues to procure biometric voter kits and is deduplicating its roughly 8.2 million-strong biometric voter registry ahead of elections. Separately, Cameroon's civil registration authority (BUNEC) is digitising civil status records and introducing a Unique Personal Identification Number, which government and technical partners state is intended eventually to align with existing identity and voter platforms. No public source confirms that the electoral register is currently linked to a broader government data exchange or interoperability layer.

Definition: Integration of tax administration and revenue collection systems data into the exchange platform
Comments: SIGIT (Integrated System for Management of Taxes) under development with GIZ support. Digital tax filing and e-taxation partially operational. General Directorate of Taxes (DGI) undergoing digital transformation. However, no evidence of full integration with a central interoperability platform.
revision_notes: Confirmed. Prior sources (BMZ Digital Transformation Center note, CSEA general digital-economy snapshot) were only loosely relevant to tax-system integration specifically. Fresh search finds the Ministry of Finance awarded the SIGIT (Système Intégré de Gestion des Impôts et Taxes) contract on 10 April 2026 to the ARABSOFT/ORADIST/C2D/DBS consortium, financed by KfW, for a 24-month implementation. SIGIT is explicitly designed to interconnect DGI with Customs, Budget and Treasury systems. As of mid-2026 the system is still in the design/installation phase (a related network-infrastructure tender remains open, deadline 10 July 2026) and is not yet operational, so 'Under development' remains the correct code, now resting on much stronger evidence. Year updated to reflect the 2026 contract award.
revised_comments: Cameroon's Directorate General of Taxes (DGI) is implementing SIGIT (Système Intégré de Gestion des Impôts et Taxes), an integrated tax and revenue management system financed by the German development bank KfW. The Ministry of Finance awarded the design, supply and installation contract in April 2026 to an ARABSOFT/ORADIST/C2D/DBS consortium, with a 24-month delivery timeline. SIGIT is designed to interconnect with Customs, Budget and Treasury systems and to provide an online taxpayer portal for filing, payment and case tracking. An accompanying network-infrastructure tender for DGI's decentralised offices remains open. The system is under active development but not yet operational, so full integration with the broader data exchange platform is not yet in place.

Definition: Whether a detailed implementation roadmap with phases, milestones, and timelines exists for data exchange development
Comments: No specific interoperability implementation roadmap found. The Civil Registration Master Plan 2018-2022 exists for CRVS but no broader data exchange roadmap with detailed milestones. PATNuC has a project implementation plan but not a published interoperability roadmap.
revision_notes: Confirmed 'No'. Original sources (a CRVS-focused journal article and a brief PATNUC blog post) gave limited detail on any data-exchange-specific roadmap. Fresh review of PATNUC's structure (per MINPOSTEL and World Bank project documents) shows it is organised around components covering digital strategy/regulation, connectivity and inclusion, and agricultural data solutions, each with its own results framework, but this is a digital-transformation and rural-connectivity programme rather than a dedicated, published, phased roadmap for cross-government data exchange/interoperability specifically. No such document was located, so the 'No' score is confirmed.
revised_comments: No dedicated implementation roadmap for cross-government data exchange has been published. Cameroon's digital transformation efforts are organised chiefly through PATNUC (Programme d'Accélération de la Transformation Numérique au Cameroun), a World Bank-financed programme structured around components for digital strategy and regulation, connectivity and inclusion, and agricultural data solutions, each with its own results framework and monitoring arrangements. This programme addresses digital inclusion and connectivity rather than setting out a specific, published, phased roadmap for interoperability or data exchange infrastructure.

Definition: Whether a formal strategy or policy document exists specifically for government data exchange and interoperability
Comments: National Digital Economy Development Strategy (2020) and SND30 (2020-2030) provide high-level digital vision. The PATNuC acceleration project (2023) furthers this. A data governance discussion was held in 2022 focusing on interoperability barriers. However, no dedicated, comprehensive data exchange interoperability strategy exists; it is referenced within broader digital/ICT strategy documents.
revision_notes: Confirmed. The original cseaafrica.org source gave only a general digital-economy snapshot rather than strategy detail. Fresh searches confirm Cameroon's National Development Strategy 2020-2030 (SND30/NDS30) sets a high-level digital vision, and PATNUC (World Bank-financed, ongoing) implements a component on digital strategy, public policy and regulation for digital inclusion and transformation. No standalone, comprehensive data-exchange/interoperability strategy document was found; the topic remains addressed within these broader digital-economy frameworks, so the code of 2 (mentioned in broader DPI/digital strategy) is confirmed.
revised_comments: Cameroon does not have a standalone strategy dedicated to government data exchange and interoperability. The topic is addressed within broader digital-transformation frameworks: the National Development Strategy 2020-2030 (SND30) sets out a high-level vision for the digital sector, and the World Bank-financed PATNUC programme includes a component on digital strategy, public policy and regulation intended to establish institutional, legal and regulatory frameworks conducive to digital-sector growth and trust. No dedicated, comprehensive interoperability strategy document with its own phased implementation plan has been published.
